text:
alex: Quick Q — I have a trace id (01f4ab3c6d2e) but need raw log lines for the request. Best fast flow: Console trace view -> logs or CLI? Also need logs from inference-api + router.

naya: If you can open the trace in Console, there's a link on the trace page that opens the 'related logs' in the Logs app. For a one-off that's easiest. For bulk/automation use the CLI.

sam: CLI recipe I've used:
```
# get request_ids from trace
redwoodctl traces get 01f4ab3c6d2e --env prod --format json \
  | jq -r '.spans[] | .tags.request_id // empty' | sort -u

# fetch logs (for each request_id)
redwoodctl logs query --env prod --service inference-api --request-id <REQID> --from -30m | jq -c '.'
```
Works across router/inference-api by changing --service. You can also omit --service to search all services but it's slower.

oliver: If you only have a trace and Console didn't show request_id tags (some old spans), try extracting span IDs and search by `trace_id` in logs:
```
redwoodctl logs query --env prod --trace-id 01f4ab3c6d2e --from -1h
```
Not all log pipelines index trace_id, though — depends on the service's logger config.

jia: Shortcuts:
- Console: Observability > Traces > paste trace id -> 'Open related logs'
- Grafana/Tempo: open trace -> 'Open in logs' icon
- If you need a permalink to send: copy the Console URL (eg https://console.redwood.ai/observability/trace/01f4ab3c6d2e)

matt: For noisy traces, use `--from`/`--to` to narrow time range and `jq` to filter by span attributes. Example:
```
redwoodctl logs query --env prod --from '2025-06-01T12:00:00Z' --to '2025-06-01T12:05:00Z' \
  --service inference-api | jq 'select(.request_id=="abc-123")'
```
